THE SPLIT PLATE / RECIPE

Creamy Sausage Spinach Pasta

Adjusted recipe for 4 servings. Use the ingredient quantities below.

YIELD4 servings
TOTAL TIME35 min
COOK METHODSee method
EST. / SERVING~510 cal | ~39g protein
KEY TO SUCCESS: BROWN HARD, BREAK SMALL. Use a meat masher to break sausage finely (kid-bite size). Big chunks distribute unevenly across containers; small crumble distributes everywhere.

Ingredients scaled from the original 8-serving recipe. Cooking times, pan size, and amounts written in the method may need adjustment.

Ingredients

PROTEIN

  • 1 1/2 lb Falls Brand Mild Italian Sausage (the 24 oz / 1.5 lb tray, buy 2)

ADULT PASTA

  • 3 servings dry Pete's Pasta Rotini (about 12 oz dry — adult pot)

Option 1

  • 1 1/2 servings dry Barilla Mini Penne (about 6 oz dry — kid pot)
  • (nothing — keep it plain)

Option 2

  • 1 1/2 servings dry Barilla Mini Penne (about 6 oz dry — kid pot)
  • (nothing — keep it plain)

SAUCE

  • 1/2 full jar Rao's Homemade Alfredo Sauce (~15 oz)
  • 1/2 additional serving Rao's Alfredo (about 4 oz from a second jar, OR substitute 1/4 cup heavy cream + 2 tbsp Parmesan)
  • Up to 1/2 cup chicken bone broth (added slowly to loosen sauce as needed)

ADULT FINISH

  • 6 oz wilted baby spinach (from the shared step, all of it)
  • Pinch of red chili flakes
  • 1/4 tsp Italian seasoning

Allergens: dairy, gluten.

AT THE PASTA POTS. Two pots cook simultaneously (Pete's for adults, Barilla for kids). After draining the sausage and building the Alfredo, split the sausage-sauce 60/40 between the two pasta pots. Adult pot gets the wilted spinach + chili flakes + Italian seasoning; kid pot stays plain.

Method

Shared base

  1. 1.BROWN THE SAUSAGE. All 3 lb in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Break apart finely with a meat masher (kid-bite size). 8-10 min until deeply browned and fond starts forming.
  2. 2.DRAIN THE FAT (NON-NEGOTIABLE). Pour the sausage into a strainer over a bowl. Discard the rendered grease. Return drained sausage to the pan. This step determines whether the meal prep stays creamy or turns oily by day 2.
  3. 3.WILT SPINACH SEPARATELY. 12 oz baby spinach in a separate pan over medium heat. 90 seconds, just until bright green. Drain, squeeze excess water. Set aside.
  4. 4.COOK TWO PASTAS SIMULTANEOUSLY. Pot 1: 6 servings dry Pete's Rotini, salted boiling water, 9-10 min al dente (adult). Pot 2: 3 servings dry Barilla Mini Penne, same timing (kid).
  5. 5.BUILD THE SAUCE. Lower heat on the sausage pan. Add the full jar of Rao's + 1 extra serving. Stir until coated. If tight, splash bone broth (2 tbsp at a time, up to 1/2 cup total). Sauce should coat the back of a spoon.

Adult — Pete's Rotini + Spinach + Heat

  1. 6.ADULT POT. Toss drained Pete's Rotini with 60% of the sausage-Alfredo from the shared pan. Fold in wilted spinach. Sprinkle a pinch of chili flakes + 1/2 tsp Italian seasoning. Toss until rotini grooves are coated.
  2. 7.PLATE ADULT. Generous scoop into a wide bowl. Rotini grooves catch the sauce + sausage + spinach. Optional: cracked black pepper + grated Parmesan.

Kid — Mini Penne + Sausage Only · Option 1

  1. 6.KID POT. Toss drained Barilla Mini Penne with 40% of the sausage-Alfredo from the shared pan. NO spinach, NO chili flakes. Stir to coat.
  2. 7.PLATE KID. Smaller bowl. Just pasta + sauce + visible sausage crumble. Looks like the cafeteria penne they already eat — no surprises.

Kid — Mini Penne + Sausage Only · Option 2

  1. 6.Skip the Alfredo on this kid's pasta entirely. Toss the drained mini penne with 1 tbsp butter + a pinch of salt + some sausage crumble. Done.

SPLIT PLATE SERVING

Adult — Pete's Rotini + Spinach + Heat: Serve the adult portion as described above.

Kid — Mini Penne + Sausage Only: Serve the kid portion as described above.

Keys to success

  • DRAIN THE FAT. After the sausage is browned, pour everything into a strainer set over a bowl. Discard the rendered fat (or save 1 tbsp for the spinach pan if you want). Return the drained meat to the pan. This is the single move that determines whether the meal prep stays creamy or turns oily by day 2.
  • COOK SPINACH SEPARATELY. Wilt 12 oz baby spinach in a separate pan over medium heat (with or without 1 tsp of the reserved sausage fat). 90 seconds — pull when bright green, not gray. Drain and squeeze excess water.

If something fails

Sauce is oily / greasy: You skipped the fat-drain step. There is no save here mid-recipe — next time, drain. For tonight, scoop visible fat off the top of the pan with a spoon and stir in 1 tbsp of fresh cream cheese to re-emulsify. Imperfect fix.

Pasta is dry by day 3 of leftovers: Add 2 tbsp of chicken bone broth or water when reheating. Microwave covered 90 sec, stir, microwave 30 sec more. Pete's pasta absorbs sauce overnight — the bone broth gives it somewhere to loosen back up.

Sausage broke into big chunks instead of fine crumble: Use a meat masher tool (or potato masher). Most home cooks use a spatula and stop mashing too early. Keep mashing for the first 4 minutes — fine crumble distributes flavor evenly across the dish.

Spinach turned gray and watery: Cooked too long OR added directly to the sauce. Wilt SEPARATELY for 90 sec, drain, squeeze. Then fold into the adult pan.

Kid won't eat the mini penne even plain: Strip 1 oz of the sausage-Alfredo from the kid pan and mix in 1 tbsp regular butter + a pinch of salt. Plain pasta + butter is the universal kid override.

Adults want more heat: Bump the chili flakes from a pinch to 1/4 tsp per adult bowl. Or stir in 1 tsp of Calabrian chili paste at the very end — that's the restaurant move.

Storage and reheating

Store: 8 containers, fridge. Pete's pasta absorbs sauce overnight — that's why the bone broth fix exists for reheating.

Reheat: Microwave covered 90 sec + a splash of chicken bone broth (or water) to loosen the sauce, stir, microwave 30 sec more. Skip the reheat-splash and the dish goes chalky by day 3.

Lasts: 4-5 days in the fridge. Freezes OK for 2 months but Pete's protein pasta texture softens slightly after freezer storage. Best fresh through day 4.

Creamy Sausage Spinach Pasta

Protein pasta is the lever, not the lean turkey. Pete's rotini absorbs the indulgence — splurge on full-fat Italian sausage + real Alfredo because the pasta's 17g protein + 7g net carbs makes the macros honest. Kids eat regular mini penne with the same sausage. Both versions are real food, neither is fake-healthy.

Make this when

You want one cook to feed the family tonight AND fill 8 lunch containers for the week. Adults get Pete's high-protein rotini with sausage + spinach + chili flakes. Kids get Barilla mini penne with sausage only — no spinach, no spice. Same pan-fond, two finishing paths.

Brands I use

Falls Brand
Old Fashioned Recipe Mild Italian Sausage (24 oz / 1.5 lb tray)
Fresh ground pork (not pre-cooked rope sausage). Renders enough fat in 8 min to need draining — that's exactly the macro-balance lever this recipe uses. Gluten-free. Buy two trays for the 3-lb batch.
Pete's Pasta
Rotini (8 oz, high protein / low carb, made in Italy)
17g protein / 7g net carbs per serving. This is the design lever — the protein/fiber in the pasta absorbs the indulgence of full-fat sausage + cream Alfredo, so the macros stay honest. DO NOT pair this pasta with lean turkey. That defeats the architecture.
Rao's
Homemade Alfredo Sauce (15 oz jar)
Real cream + Parmesan + butter, no flour thickener, no preservatives. The full-fat sauce is the point — the protein pasta makes the macros work.
Barilla
Classic Mini Penne (1 lb box)
Kid pasta. Mini penne is the cafeteria-familiar shape — kids accept it instantly. Non-GMO, durum wheat. 9-10 min al dente, same window as Pete's.
Marketside (Walmart)
Fresh Baby Spinach (11 oz clamshell)
Pre-washed, pre-trimmed. Wilts in 90 sec. Adult-pan-only ingredient — kids consistently reject it, save your spinach and your peace.
